description.value: The study investigated how cognitive reappraisal of positive and negative emotional images affects vmPFC activity and whether vmPFC activation tracks subjective and normative emotional value.

design.value: Two independent experimental samples of human participants performed a cognitive reappraisal task while undergoing fMRI; Exp1 included younger adults and Exp2 included older and younger adults as a replication sample.

description.value: After each trial, participants rated how positive or negative they felt after having implemented the strategy.
Exp2 participants scored at 27 or higher.

name.value: participants' own trial-by-trial ratings of the valence of stimuli

source_definition.value: participants' own trial-by-trial ratings of the valence of stimuli

description.value: Participants in Exp1 were 31 younger adults between the ages of 19 and 40 years.

medical_condition.value: no history of psychiatric or neurological problems or contraindications to fMRI scanning

description.value: Exp2 comprised 22 younger adults between the ages of 19 and 33 years.
Exp2 comprised 20 older adults between the ages of 59 and 73 years.

task_description.value: Participants were presented with images from the International Affective Picture System and were asked to either regulate their emotions using cognitive reappraisal or to experience their emotions naturally.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to imagine themselves as an objective observer to the situation depicted or to imagine the event as having no personal relevance to them; for the Experience condition, participants were instructed to experience their emotions naturally.

stimuli.value: Images from the International Affective Picture System, categorized as positive, negative, or neutral based on normative IAPS ratings.

task_description.value: Replication sample drawn from a previously published study using a nearly identical cognitive reappraisal task.

description.value: Functional data were acquired using a gradient-echo inverse-spiral pulse sequence; 30 axial slices parallel to the AC–PC plane; FOV = 256 mm; flip angle = 60°; each run contained 288 volumes, with the first six volumes discarded.
Exp2 used 34 slices, flip angle = 90°, voxel size = 3.75 × 3.75 × 3.8 mm, and each run contained 238 volumes; the first six volumes were discarded.
A high-resolution inversion-recovery prepared SPGR anatomical image was used for normalization and coregistration of the functional data, with whole brain coverage and 1 × 1 × 1 mm voxels.
fMRI preprocessing included motion correction, brain extraction, spatial smoothing, high-pass filtering, and normalization to standard space.

steps.value: spatial smoothing using an isotropic Gaussian kernel of 6 mm (FWHM)
registration to participant's main structural image using six degrees of freedom
registration to standard space using 12 degrees of freedom
runs with >5 volumes with movement of >1 mm in any direction were discarded

model_settings.value: First-level models included one regressor for each trial type and nuisance regressors for initial picture presentation and response period; parametric models included trial-by-trial ratings, an orthogonalized main-effect regressor, and a quadratic regressor.

estimator.value: local autocorrelation correction; fixed-effects model across runs within participant; mixed-effects analysis (FLAME 1) across participants

model_settings.value: Valence and condition were modeled as fixed effects and each participant as a random effect; variance components covariance structure.

multiple_comparison_method.value: full whole-brain correction; cluster-corrected significance threshold

model_representation_notes.value: First-level models corrected for local autocorrelation; nuisance regressors modeled the initial presentation of the picture and the response period; all regressors were convolved with a standard double-gamma hemodynamic response function.

interpretations.value: Negative regulation activated regions of the prefrontal cortex including the inferior frontal gyrus, the middle frontal gyrus, and the superior frontal gyrus. In addition, regulating negative emotion led to increased activation in the posterior cingulate and the angular gyrus.

title.value: Effect of reappraisal, IAPS rating, and pvmPFC activation on behavior

footer.value: GLM revealed that IAPS normative rating, condition, and an IAPS normative-rating-by-condition interaction predicted valence ratings. In addition, there was also a significant relationship between pvmPFC activation and behavior. *Significant.

description.value: Behavioral GLM parameter estimates for experiment number, IAPS normative ratings, condition, their interaction, and pvmPFC activation.
